details: Bitcoin surged to above $65,500, gaining nearly 3% in the past 24 hours, following reports of a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran. This deal, which includes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, has significantly reduced instability in the Middle East and reignited investor risk appetite across global financial markets, including digital assets. The wider crypto market capitalization also saw broad gains.
title: US-Iran Deal Boosts Risk Appetite, Lifts Crypto Markets

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) raised its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.25% (or 2.4% as per some reports) around June 11-12, 2026. This marks its first interest rate hike since September 2023, driven by inflation concerns, particularly those exacerbated by the Middle East conflict. This tightening of monetary policy by a major central bank increases monetary policy risk, reduces liquidity, and is likely to exert pressure on crypto and DeFi markets, potentially impacting adoption and speculative token performance.
title: ECB Raises Interest Rates Amid Inflation Concerns

details: Bitcoin is trading near the $65,600 mark, with its price remaining range-bound due to weakening institutional demand. Bitcoin ETFs recorded $316 million in net outflows last week, marking the fifth consecutive week of such outflows. Despite this, long-term investors appear to be holding their positions. Markets are now anticipating signals from the upcoming US Federal Reserve policy meeting.
title: Weakening Institutional Demand Keeps Bitcoin Range-Bound
